chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from Al-Hasan al-Sayqalī said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it sufficient for me to recite only Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in the obligatory prayer if I am in a hurry or something hastens me? He said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَة الْكِتَاب: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite only Surah Al-Fatiha in obligatory prayer when in a hurry?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Al-Hasan al-Sayqal asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether reciting only Sūrat al-Fātiḥah suffices for the obligatory prayer when time is short or one is hurried. The Imam’s affirmative response, 'There is no harm,' establishes the permissibility of this concession, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*rukhas*) in ritual worship during times of necessity or haste.
